title: Pack six books in the case so its lid shuts
instruction: Pack all six books flat in the case and close its lid.
context: Done by: library technicians, bookbinding workers and bookshop stockers (O*NET 25-4031, 51-5113, 53-7065). A hardback is thicker at the spine, so books are stacked spine to fore-edge, thick edges shared between the sides; a same-way stack leans and a lid shut on it crushes spines. The rule is not stated; the level check carries it. Unlike TK-JDWDKK (turn each tote to stack) and TK-VF9Z7F (stated carton pattern), the robot must count spines across the stack.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view, heights are above the table top, and the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Book case (fixed, grey painted plywood): a floor 136 mm front to back, 110 mm wide and 6 mm thick, centred 34 cm in front of the arm bases and 1.5 cm left of the midline; a rail 6 mm thick and 30 mm tall across each end of the floor, their inner faces 124 mm apart; a post 6 x 8 mm at each corner, 120 mm tall; the long left and right sides are open. Lid (dark grey painted plywood, 136 x 110 x 5 mm, 0.10 kg, with a 12 x 12 mm lip along its free edge): hinged along the case's right-hand top edge, 4 cm right of the midline and 120 mm up. It starts open, resting on its stop 29 degrees out past upright; tipped about 4 degrees past upright toward the case, it falls shut onto the posts, its underside 114 mm above the case floor. Six hardback books (loose, rigid, 0.12 kg each), each 100 x 64 mm: a 12 mm board-and-page slab with a 14 mm wide black spine band along one long edge, on two strips 5 mm wide under its long edges, 10 mm deep under the spine and 2 mm under the fore-edge (22 mm thick at the spine, 14 mm at the fore-edge), so a lone book visibly leans 7.7 degrees, spine edge up. The fore-edge strip is cream, like page edges. Covers: red, blue, green, ochre, purple, teal. Lot A: the red book in the case, centred 34 cm in front and 2.5 cm left of the midline, length front to back, spine to the left. The others lie on the table, length left to right, spines toward the robot, centred at: blue 36 cm in front and 21 cm left, green 36 and 32, ochre 36 and 43, purple 46 and 26, teal 46 and 37. Lot B: as lot A, but the red book's spine is to the right. Lot C: as lot A, but the teal book lies on the red book in the case, spine also to the left (the pair leans about 15 degrees), and its table spot is empty. Nothing else is on the table. Trials are run on lots A, B and C and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial from a photo, a ruler and a phone level, after the robot has let go (no gripper, finger or wrist within 5 mm of any book or the lid). Packed: all six books lying flat (each one's covers within 30 degrees of level, none on edge or end) inside the case (each book's whole outline between the inner faces of the two end rails and within the floor's 110 mm width, 1 mm tolerance, nothing below the floor), no part of any book higher than the shut lid's underside (114 mm above the case floor), the top book's covers within 4 degrees of level, and every book still (moving under 1 cm/s). 1.0: packed and the lid shut (within 1.5 degrees of lying flat on its posts, its free edge within about 3 mm), held for 1 s, which ends the trial. 0.5: packed at the last step, but the lid still open. 0 otherwise: a book left out, overhanging the case or standing on edge, a top book leaning more than 4 degrees (for example four spines on one side and two on the other, which leans about 15 degrees), the lid resting on a book, a book or the lid still held. Trials are run on each of lots A, B and C and averaged.
reset_notes: Take the books out and lay them back on their table spots, length left to right, spines toward the robot. Lot A: put the red book in the case, spine left; lot B: spine right; lot C: red book spine left with the teal book on it, also spine left. Tip the lid out onto its open stop. Nothing is consumed. Run with -E object_jitter=0 and --epochs 3.
fidelity: Rigid boxes. The spine swell is exaggerated so it shows: each book is a slab on a 10 mm strip under the spine and a 2 mm strip under the fore-edge (real swell is a few mm), so stacks lean in steps; real books are soft. The case's long sides are open so fingers reach. The lid falls shut by its own weight. Masses and friction are simulator values. The lots stop a fixed habit, not a memorised replay of all three.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A, B and C); demo: 1.0 in each lot
